output.title: The Skill of Being Wrong
output.excerpt: A short essay about the one habit that, if everyone practiced it, would improve nearly everything. Why this essay exists Almost every large problem humans face is not a problem of resources or intelligence. We have enough food to feed everyone. We have enough energy technology to avoid the worst…

summary: The Skill of Being Wrong is an essay arguing that epistemic humility is a practical, learnable skill and perhaps the highest-leverage idea for the greatest number of people. It makes the case that certainty is a feeling rather than evidence, that strong opinions are best held weakly and tested in disagreement, and that honesty builds the trust cooperation depends on, closing with a handful of daily habits.
